newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Philips 1996 result ravaged by charges.
newsitem.headline: Philips 1996 result ravaged by charges.

text.p: Philips Electronics NV on Thursday reported a 1996 net loss of 590 million guilders ($312.8 million) after booking net extraordinary charges of over 1.3 billion guilders in the year.
The company reported a net profit from normal operations during the year of 723 million guilders and the dividend was held unchanged at 1.60 guilders per common share.
"The year 1996 was a severe disappointment, due to a much lower level of sales growth and costs which grew faster than sales," Philips said in a statement.
However, the company said it anticipated its current businesses would continue to grow in 1997.
"We had to take substantial restructuring charges, and we are committed to a return to profitability and to the achievement of a positive cash flow of over one billion guilders," it said.
Philips chairman Cor Boonstra acknowledged the effect of the extraordinaries and added Philips had not responded quickly enough to market conditions.

"Part of this decline was caused by gearing up our organisation for growth which did not materialise. We were simply not quick enough in reacting to the market," said Boonstra in his first annual statement since becoming Philips' chairman in October.
"We do not blame the markets, nor our competitors, but rather take full responsibility for our lack of speed," he said.

Charges taken during the year included an 800 million pre-tax charge to restructure the Sound and Vision unit as well as another one billion guilders -- of which 600 million related to loss making German unit Grundig.
